rationale: Both texts tell the same two interlocking stories in the same order -- a synagogue leader's daughter, interrupted by a woman bleeding "for twelve years" who touches Jesus's clothing -- and share near-identical sayings, checked directly against this app's own shipped BSB text: "The girl is not dead, but asleep" (Matthew 9:24) against "The child is not dead, but asleep" (Mark 5:39), followed in both by "they laughed at Him." The differences are just as checkable. Matthew never names the father, calling him only "a synagogue leader" (9:18), where Mark names him ("A synagogue leader named Jairus," 5:22); Matthew's father says "My daughter has just died" (9:18), where Mark's says "My little daughter is near death" (5:23) and the death is reported later by messengers (5:35); and Mark carries material Matthew does not have at all -- the physicians (5:26), Jesus asking "Who touched My garments?" (5:30), the three disciples (5:37), "Talitha koum!" (5:41), and the girl's age (5:42). Graded parallel because no citation links the two accounts, and strong rather than explicit because the shared sequence is substantial while these differences are real; which account depends on which is reported in the lesson, not decided by this connection.
